newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hits Japanese vessels with port surcharge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hits Japanese vessels with port surcharge.

text.p: The U.S. Maritime Commission on Wednesday said it would impose $100,000 surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports in retaliation for what it said were unfair Japanese port practices.

"The Federal Maritime Commission, in response to unfavorable conditions in the foreign oceanborne trade between the United States and Japan, is imposing $100,000 per-voyage fees on liner vessels operated by Japanese carriers calling at United States ports," the commission said in its final ruling.
The commission said the surcharge would become effective on April 14.
By refusing to license non-Japanese companies to perform stevedoring or terminal operating services, the Japanese government was discriminating against U.S. carriers, the commission said.
Repeated diplomatic efforts over the last several years by the Unitee States and other trading partners failed to bring about necessary reforms, it added.

"The commission further found that the government of Japan, through its licensing practices and other support, appeared to protect the dominant position of the Japan Harbor Transportation Association (JHTA), the trade organization that wields broad control over the Japanese harbor services industry," the order said.

The commission said the surcharge will be imposed each time a vessel owned or operated by Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK enters a U.S. port from abroad, but not from another U.S. port.
"The fee represents a measured approach to Japanese port conditions, crafted to respond firmly to Japanese practices without disrupting U.S. trade and ocean commerce," the commission said.
The fee was a "significant amount" but not enough to have and adverse impact on U.S. ports and shippers, it said.
The commission said that if Japan moves to retaliate against U.S. lines, the level of fees on Japanese carriers would be increased proportionally.
